A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FIRE-Bench, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained experiments and appendix material can be matched despite renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original agent evaluations on 30 tasks, error and contamination analyses, and human evaluations of tree parsing and claim extraction.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds agent evaluations on 10 cross-domain tasks and a contamination analysis covering 40 tasks.

M1.justification: The research-problem tree, parent-node task selection, automated extraction, and claim-level scoring procedures remain unchanged. The retained appendix prompts are identical apart from headings; broader application and proposed future training uses do not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Section 5.5 and Appendix D add evaluations on five computer-vision/vision-language tasks and five neural-network-analysis tasks, substantially broadening v1's LLM-behavior coverage. The additional 60 parsed papers are explicitly unevaluated. The core Hallucination Awareness question also adds intermediate-reasoning auditing and changes source attribution, although its numerical results remain unchanged and rerunning is not documented.

E2.justification: The original comparison retains OpenHands with o4-mini and gpt-5, Codex with gpt-5-medium, and Claude Code with Sonnet-4. The new cross-domain experiment uses three existing configurations, omitting Claude Code there for budget reasons; no comparator is added or removed from the retained experiments.

E3.justification: Section 5.5 introduces a reported 60-minute budget for the neural-network extension, whereas the retained core protocol states that no hard runtime limit is imposed. Core scoring, hardware, and model configurations remain unchanged; the extension should not be interpreted as a same-setting performance comparison.

E4.justification: Appendix E extends the difficulty-conditioned contamination analysis from 30 to 40 tasks. Section 5.5 adds qualitative diagnoses involving dataset dependencies and execution timeouts. The medical-bias case-study table mainly redisplays an analysis already present in v1.

E5.justification: Section 5.1 newly summarizes run variability using median coefficients of variation and the frequency of standard deviations reaching the mean. Three-run mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting remains unchanged, including for the new extension; no increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: Core numerical table entries are retained, but Table 11 adds results for 10 tasks and three agents, averaging 23.4, 13.3, and 30.2 F1 for OpenHands/o4-mini, OpenHands/gpt-5, and Codex respectively. Table 12 adds 40-task contamination results. Section 5.5's statement that all three extension averages are below 25 contradicts Codex's reported 30.2.

T1.justification: The tree definitions, extractor equation, and difficulty rubric are retained. Added explanations about parent-node difficulty and author-aligned research trees are conceptual clarifications, with no new formal derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The contribution scope expands from a 30-task LLM-behavior benchmark to a claimed 100-paper living release with 40 executed tasks. The introduction newly claims a reusable formalism validated across 100 papers and 10+ subfields, while the abstract and conclusion position the benchmark as a foundation for training research agents. The original limited-success finding remains.

C2.justification: v2 adds a substantive domain-dependent interpretation: dependency management and implementation/execution become bottlenecks on heavier tasks, extending v1's emphasis on planning and conclusion formation. It also argues that required execution structurally mitigates memorization and removes the conclusion's inference that rare alternative findings indicate a lack of creativity.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds a catalog link for the claimed 100-paper release, including extracted trees for 60 unevaluated papers. Section 6 describes versioning, a public leaderboard, and community submissions. Existing prompts, hardware details, and scoring models are retained; cost-estimation details are relocated rather than newly disclosed.

R1.justification: Table 1 revises the benchmark-family comparison, separating method replication from metric-driven discovery. Appendix B adds a benchmark-scale comparison including MLGym, and the extension introduces its source-paper citations. Most other reference edits update publication metadata without changing the cited work.

P1.justification: The abstract and conclusion are rewritten, an explicit contribution list and explanatory passages are added, and cost methodology moves into an appendix. The main section sequence and most existing technical prose and appendix content remain intact. Title, author-order, publication, and acknowledgment text also change.

P2.justification: The compact benchmark-comparison figure becomes a full-width transposed table. New tables present a task example, the existing medical-bias case study, benchmark scale, extension sources and results, and extended contamination results. The cost table moves to the appendix, while the workflow, error-distribution, and difficulty figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The executed cross-domain extension supplies useful evidence about applicability and failure modes beyond LLM-behavior research, and the expanded contamination analysis strengthens diagnostic coverage. These gains are limited by sparse extension-protocol details and new reporting problems: Section 5.5 claims all extension averages are below 25 despite Codex scoring 30.2 in Table 11. The core method and evaluator validation remain unchanged.
